analysis: Examined ModelDownloader+Download.swift (base vs head) and the new test file ModelDownloadProgressTests.swift. The production change is confined to progress and UI plumbing in downloadManifestModel (head lines 129-166). The per-file task closure is factored into a shared `transfer` closure that calls progress.start(label:) before downloadManifestFileWithResume and progress.update/complete in the same order as before. The render task is now awaited after cancel (`await renderTask.value`) at head lines 162 and 166, so no frame lands below the final summary. Security-relevant controls are unchanged: validateArtifactManifest, verifyRevisionAndRepairReceipt, reuseVerifiedFiles, fileMatches (size plus SHA-256), ensureAvailableCapacity, the staging directory, the .part resume, finalizeStagedManifest (aggregate hash check and publish) and the catch-path staging cleanup. The weight-integrity and download-verification path (A-004, T-012, T-027) is not affected. No new network, filesystem, key, attestation or authorization surface appears. The `@Sendable` closure captures self, progress and model, which are the same values the old per-task closures captured. Availability: awaiting renderTask.value should terminate because the loop checks Task.isCancelled every 250ms. The remaining question is whether `ManifestDownloadProgress.start`, `ProgressRenderer` and its `isTTY`/`terminalSize`/`output` initializer exist in non-supplied source; this affects only build correctness. The test file is test-only. It writes nothing to disk and uses an in-memory virtual terminal and a captured output sink. It has no secrets or prompt data and does not touch the prefix-cache threat T-041. No findings.
